newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli official threatens to quit over probe.
newsitem.headline: Israeli official threatens to quit over probe.

text.p: Israel's deputy finance minister threatened on Wednesday to resign over the findings of a corruption probe into Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government.
But the deputy minister, David Magen, said he would meet the head of his Gesher faction, Foreign Minister David Levy, on Thursday before making a final decision on stepping down.

Earlier, Magen said he had considered quitting his post for weeks but Netanyahu's response to a report 10 days ago by public prosecutors on the short-lived appointment of an attorney general in January was the last straw.

"The reasons for my resignation, which have to do with political and parliamentary developments I foresee, will be explained at a later date in the proper framework," Magen said in a letter obtained by Reuters.
Within hours, Magen appeared to backtrack, telling Reuters: "I will be meeting Levy tomorrow and I decided to withhold my resignation for the time being."
Gesher's departure could shake Netanyahu's 66-member coalition but there were no signs Levy or other legislators would join Magen.
Netanyahu lashed out at the media and opposition in a speech only moments after prosecutors, citing insufficient evidence, decided on April 20 not to charge him with fraud and breach of trust.
Prosecutors however said there were "real suspicions" about his role in the influence-peddling scandal.

"The straw that broke the camel's back was the prime minister's horror show on television following publication of the decision," said Magen, whose faction is part of a right-wing bloc with Netanyahu's Likud party.

Police who conducted the corruption probe had recommended indicting Netanyahu, Justice Minister Tzachi Hanegbi, Netanyahu's director-general Avigdor Lieberman and key legislator Aryeh Deri in connection with the appointment of Likud political crony Roni Bar-On as attorney-general.
Prosecutors announced a 75-page decision to charge Deri alone but petitioners have asked the High Court of Justice to order indictments against the prime minister.

Netanyahu admitted making mistakes in the appointment, which Channel One Television alleged was part of a plea-bargain deal for Deri already on trial for corruption. But Netanyahu said he had been vindicated of any criminal act.
